question: A man makes a monthly payment equal to 25% of his monthly salary towards debt repayment. He spends 52% of the remaining salary and saves ₹288. His monthly salary (in ₹) is
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the total monthly salary be 100%.

Remaining salary after 25% debt repayment = 100% − 25% = 75%.

Savings % = (100% − 52%) of 75% = 48% of 75% = 36%.

Given that 36% of total salary = ₹288.

Total salary (100%) = 288 ÷ 36 × 100 = 8 × 100 = 800.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹800.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Debt repayment = 25% of monthly salary

Amount spent from remaining salary = 52%

Total amount saved = ₹288

**Formula Used:**

Savings = Total Salary × (Remaining % after debt) × (Remaining % after spending)

 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 
• 

 
 Salary = 100%

 
 Debt = 25%

 
 Remaining = 75%

 
 Spend = 39%

 
 Save = 36%

 36% = ₹288

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the total monthly salary be x.

⇒ After paying 25% towards debt, remaining salary = x × (100 − 25) ÷ 100 = 0.75x

⇒ He spends 52% of the remaining salary, so he saves (100 − 52) = 48% of the remaining amount.

⇒ Savings = 48% of 0.75x

⇒ Savings = (48 ÷ 100) × 0.75x = 0.36x

⇒ Given that his savings = ₹288

⇒ 0.36x = 288

⇒ x = 288 ÷ 0.36

⇒ x = 28800 ÷ 36

⇒ x = 800

**∴ The correct answer is ₹800.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Application

When a percentage is applied to a remaining amount, the current balance acts as a new 100% base. The formula is Final Value = Initial Value × (1 − p₁/100) × (1 − p₂/100).

Fraction Conversion Method

Converting percentages to fractions speeds up calculations. 25% = 1/4 (leaving 3/4 remaining) and 48% = 12/25. Thus, Savings = Total × 3/4 × 12/25 = Total × 9/25.

Tree Diagram Approach

Visualizing total values as branches (e.g., 100 splitting into 25 and 75, then 75 splitting into 39 and 36) helps prevent errors when consecutive percentages are calculated on remaining parts rather than the initial total.
